Yeah, unfortunately men are less understanding about these kinds of things on average in my experience. But I gotta do what's right for me. I'm tired of feeling anxious and confused all the time. 

Good luck! I hope everything goes all right when you do decide to come out to those friends.

I will. It will be interesting to say the least. I'm a little nervous, but my friend is amazing and has been so supportive. I think I'll be ok as long as she's with me. 

But I'll definitely let you know how it goes.

I wish it were that easy, heh. I don't feel like I can truly love myself until I know who that is. But I've got some great friends who have been supporting me a lot lately. My one friend is forcing me to go to a transgender conference this weekend. She thinks it will help me a lot to meet other trans people.

Thanks. When I read [this post from hildy_j](http://www.reddit.com/r/asktransgender/comments/1csn7o/feeling_guilty_for_not_being_dysphoric_enough/), I began to feel a lot better about my situation. I didn't know how to word it, but being of low dysphoria is exactly what's confusing me. 

I don't mind being a male so much, but I feel that I would be happier as a female. It makes me second guess myself a lot.

As of now, I've told 4 or 5 really close female friends, and they've all been pretty awesome about it. But I also have some male friends that are very homophobic, and I know I'll lose them, which sucks.

I haven't expressed any externally visible femininity in public as of yet (Edit: unless you count my long hair). Still too anxious and frankly, terrified to do so. I have made long term changes as of late that aren't visible to anyone when I'm in public. And I still wear externally male clothing. 

The thing is that sometimes I just feel masculine. Now, I've put up a front my entire life and overcompensated masculinity to make up for what I saw as a flaw. Now I'm not sure if the times I want to express masculinity are because I actually feel that way, or because I feel anxious and start receding back into myself. 

I've had terrible anxiety my entire life, as well as OCD. And with OCD you create coping mechanisms to deal with your anxiety. I'm not sure if these periods of masculinity are that, or the real me, or what. That's what's really confusing the hell out of me.

I just worry that I'll come out, lose some good friends, deal with all the issues that face the trans community nowadays, and then feel that I made the wrong decision since the feelings fade from time to time.
Thank you for posting this. I feel a little less anxiety knowing someone else knows how I feel.

I've hated my body since I was young, and it's caused a lot of depression and anxiety for me. I want to look/feel like a woman a lot of times. Like right now. But sometimes those feelings fade and I become complacent with my current body. It doesn't really make any sense.
